### **B. Support Vector Regression**

Support Vector Machines support both Linear and Non-Linear Regression, commonly referred to as SVR [4]. Instead of trying to fit the largest possible street between two classes while limiting margin violations, SVR [5] tries to fit as many instances on the street while limiting margin violations. The width of the street is controlled by the hyperparameter epsilon. Here, we use the kernel trick to predict data. The kernels used [6] in our case are RBF/Gaussian kernel and Polynomial kernel. We evaluate the metrics on the two kernels and select the one with the least Mean Squared Error (MSE) and the highest R2 score.
